Subject: Prompt sets & eval harness integration — onboarding plan

Team — kicking this off for Acme Retail (DEAL-5821). Goal: get their quality monitoring pipeline healthy for the initial rollout (homepage search generator + product description rewrite). High level asks and proposed timeline below. Attaching initial prompt set CSV and the integration notes.

Deliverables (first 4 weeks):
- Finalize prompt sets v1 (customer + Redwood review) — owner: Marissa
- Wire eval harness into Acme's staging environment (CI hook + reporting) — owner: Karthik
- Regression alert rules and canary/rollback policy draft — owner: Grace
- SOW and milestone signoff (customer legal) — owner: Lauren

Key definitions and constraints:
- Canary window: 2k production requests or 48 hours, whichever comes first.
- Regression alert triggers: 5% absolute drop in top-1 relevance OR a 10% increase in hallucination rate on the prompt set (detailed metrics in eval_harness_integration.md).
- Rollback policy: automated routing to fallback model variant + paged on-call if regression persists for two consecutive canary windows.

Next steps by Tuesday 18 Apr:
1) Marissa: send the first prompt CSV to Acme for review (see prompt_sets_v1.csv).
2) Karthik: confirm the CI hook format and sample payload; share a workspace link for the harness.
3) Grace: draft alert thresholds and escalation flow (include PagerDuty play).
4) Lauren: share SOW draft with Legal and Acme.

I expect we'll need a 30-45m kickoff with Acme once the prompt set is stable — propose Thu 14 Apr or Fri 15 Apr.

Lauren
Sr. Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Elena — confirming Thu 14 Apr 10:00 PT. Quick notes in response to the security + rollback questions, copied for Acme: 

- Fallback model variant: by default Redwood will route to a previously-verified model version that has the same API schema (example: gptx-search-v1 -> gptx-search-v1-stable). That variant is provisioned with identical shard types but may be configured with a lower token budget (controls cost) and slightly different temperature/decoding settings. Latency delta typically <= 30ms in our staging tests; we'll confirm for Acme's region on the call.

- Paging behavior: high-severity regression alerts are configurable to page both Redwood on-call and the customer's on-call. We'll include a PagerDuty playbook in the escalation flow. Paged alerts require a threshold breach persisting for two consecutive canary windows before automatic page (to reduce noise).

- Data handling: the eval harness can run without persisting raw prompt text; we provide a hashed prompt ID and aggregated metrics by default. If Acme needs the raw prompts for debugging, we can set up an auditable storage bucket with KMS encryption and short TTL. We'll include the data-flow diagram in the Drive folder.

Action items for the call tomorrow:
- Karthik: bring a short demo of the CI hook (20m).
- Grace: walk through the proposed alert thresholds and the rollback timeline (10m).
- Marissa: review prompt ownership and approval workflow with Elena (5m).

-Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
